claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 29-38: `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");` then `order.Status = "cancelled"; await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled"); return order;`. No read of order.Status anywhere in the method. Code block in section 5 matches the source character-for-character.

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 has exactly two cancel tests (lines 46, 58): NewOrder seeds Status="new" and asserts "cancelled"; UnknownOrder asserts KeyNotFoundException for id 999. Neither reads FakeNotifier.Sent; no test seeds "shipped". Lines 65-67 comment: "No test here cancels a `shipped` order. The suite is green". `dotnet test DonHang.Tests` at stage-1: Passed 5, Failed 0. git grep -i cancel in DonHang.Tests finds no other file.

story-example.md@stage-1 line 5: "hủy đơn hàng chưa thanh toán của mình"; AC3 (l.14-15): "Khi đơn ở trạng thái `paid`, `shipped` hoặc `cancelled`, nút \"Hủy đơn\" không hiện."; AC4 (l.16-17): "trả về 403 và không thay đổi gì"; AC5 (l.18-19): "lần thứ hai trả về 409"; DoD l.24: "Có test tự động cho mọi tiêu chí chấp nhận ở trên."

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 contains 5 tests: three PlaceOrderAsync, CancelOrderAsync_NewOrder_SetsStatusCancelled, CancelOrderAsync_UnknownOrder_Throws. None seeds paid/shipped/cancelled, none involves another customer (403) or a second cancel (409).

Review practice stated by the outline itself (track.yaml outline items 1-3, near-verbatim); no versioned official doc governs it and the lesson hedges item 3 ("may be passing"). Treated as the lesson's method, not a factual claim.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and overstated: a test seeded with a cancelled order and asserting "cancelled" does not pass "whatever the service does" — it fails if the service throws, returns a different Order, or sets another status. It only passes when the service leaves the status untouched (the bug the quiz q4 scenario describes). Same absolute wording in quiz q4 explanation.correct (en and vi: "nó qua dù service làm gì").
issues.fix: Replace with: "passes even if the service never changes the status." In quiz q4 explanation.correct use "so it passed even though the service never changed the status" / vi "nên nó qua dù service không hề đổi trạng thái". Add the sentence to claims (kind behavior, section 4).

issues.text: Comparative ranking ("cheaper") not established in the body; section 4 only says such tests are "worth asking about before the merge, not after a bug report". Summary line 5 introduces a cost comparison with no support.
issues.quote: Asking for a missing test before the merge is cheaper than finding the gap after a bug report.
issues.fix: Replace line 5 with: "A missing test is worth asking for before the merge, not after a bug report: without it, nothing fails when that behavior breaks."

issues.text: "without anyone noticing" is absolute; people (QA, users, reviewers) can notice. What the lesson can support is that no test fails.
issues.quote: A missing test means the next change can break that behavior without anyone noticing.
issues.fix: Change to: "A missing test means the next change can break that behavior and the build stays green." Apply the same wording to misconception 2 and quiz q2 explanation.b if kept consistent.

issues.text: Unlisted code fact: "`OrderServiceTests` uses fresh fakes in every test". True at stage-1 (every test does `new FakeOrderRepository()` / `new FakeNotifier()`), but it is a claim about the repository and is not in the ledger. Rated minor because it is verified and restates a prerequisite.
issues.quote: `OrderServiceTests` uses fresh fakes in every test
issues.fix: Add a claim to .meta.json: kind fact, section 1, source_hint DonHang.Tests/Services/OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 lines 14-15, 27-28, 40, 48-50, 60.

issues.text: "diff" is not in my known_vocab and is not defined. I can guess it means the changed files of the pull request, but I have to guess. It returns in section 4 ("A test file in the diff") and in quiz q1 option b.
issues.quote: A reviewer who counts files sees a test file in the diff and is satisfied.
issues.fix: Replace "the diff" with "the files the pull request changes" in sections 2 and 4 and in q1 option b / explanation b.

issues.text: "green" (build is green, suite is green) is jargon I do not know. Also "build" in my vocab is the Flutter build/layout/paint step, so "the build" here (and in section 4 and summary line 5) is ambiguous for me: which build, and what makes it green?
issues.quote: The build is green and every test passes.
issues.fix: At first use, write "The project compiles and every test passes (the build is green)." so both words are explained in plain terms, and keep that meaning for later uses.

issues.text: "suite" (test suite) is not in my known_vocab. I think it means all tests together, but it is never said. Used in section 5 prose, the code comment, and quiz q2/q3/q4.
issues.quote: The comment at the end of the file says the same thing: the suite is green, and a `shipped` order still gets through.
issues.fix: At the first use in prose, say "the suite (all the tests in the project)", or replace "the suite" with "all the tests" in prose and quiz.

issues.text: "test coverage" is not in my known_vocab and is not defined. The misconception depends on it, and quiz q2 repeats it in the misconception field.
issues.quote: A PR that touches a test file has adequate test coverage for what it changed.
issues.fix: Rephrase as "A PR that touches a test file has tests for everything it changed." and use the same wording in quiz q2 misconception.

issues.text: Core concepts says a test that cannot fail "checks nothing". Here the `new`-order test is called one that "cannot fail", but it looks correct to me: the story allows cancelling a `new` order. I cannot tell if the reviewer should ask to change this test, or keep it and ask for a separate `shipped` test. It also mixes with the section 4 example (seeded already cancelled), which really is broken.
issues.quote: The first test also cannot fail on the most important point: if the method cancelled every order whatever its status, it would still pass.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after it: "That test is right for the `new` item and should stay; the problem is that the `shipped` item has no test of its own, unlike the section 4 example, where the test itself is wrong."

issues.text: The author's reply does not say they also changed `CancelOrderAsync`. If only a test was added and it passes against the version shown, it is already wrong; there is nothing to ask about "failing first". The suggested answer ("before the check was added") assumes a check I was never told about.
issues.quote: The author answers your question about `shipped` orders: "I added a test, `CancelOrderAsync_ShippedOrder_IsRefused`, and it passes."
issues.fix: Make the reply say: "I added a status check to `CancelOrderAsync` and a test, `CancelOrderAsync_ShippedOrder_IsRefused`, and it passes."

issues.text: Criterion 3 is about a cancel button not showing, and 4/5 are about 403/409 responses. I stopped at step 2: should a test for a button or a status code even be in `OrderServiceTests`? The expected result says "none" but not whether that is the right place to look.
issues.quote: For each, look for a test in `OrderServiceTests` that checks it.
issues.fix: Add to the expected result for step 2 one sentence saying the task is only whether `OrderServiceTests` has any test for these, wherever such a test would later live.

issues.text: The code comment names "the reading-a-300-line-pr lesson", a lesson I have not read. For a moment I thought the gap belongs to another lesson, not this one.
issues.quote: the gap the reading-a-300-line-pr lesson is about.
issues.fix: In the prose after the block, add half a sentence: "the comment names a later lesson that returns to this same gap."

issues.text: I re-read this twice; "On the status," at the start of the sentence is unclear to me.
issues.quote: On the status, it checks what the fake already holds, not what the code under review does.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "The status it checks is the one the fake already held, not one the code under review set."

issues.text: The story allows cancelling unpaid orders, so `paid` orders should be refused too, but the situation and the suggested reviewer comment only talk about `shipped`. I wondered why `paid` is skipped.
issues.quote: But the story this work belongs to says a customer can cancel an order that has not been paid yet, and some orders have already shipped.
issues.fix: Add one short clause in section 5 saying `shipped` is used as the clearest case and a `paid` order has the same gap.

issues.text: q2: option d ("the PR changed no test files at all") contradicts the statement itself, which says the PR changes `OrderServiceTests`, so I can drop it without understanding the lesson.
issues.quote: False, because the PR changed no test files at all.
issues.fix: Replace d with a plausible wrong reason, e.g. "False, because tests with a fake repository never count as tests."

issues.text: q3: options b (test length) and c (test name) are not plausible, so it is really a choice between a and d.
issues.quote: Is the new test shorter than the other tests?
issues.fix: Replace b with a plausible but wrong question, e.g. "Does the test also check that a notification is sent?"

issues.text: q4: the correct option is near-verbatim from section 4 ("checks what the fake already holds"), and b/c/d talk about timeouts, build servers and .NET versions, which the lesson never mentions, so I can pick a by elimination.
issues.quote: The test checked what the fake returned, not the service
issues.fix: Replace one distractor with a lesson-based wrong idea, e.g. "The test used a fake instead of the real repository".

issues.text: q5: the correct option repeats the section 5 sentence "if the method cancelled every order whatever its status, it would still pass", so I can match words instead of understanding.
issues.quote: It would still pass if every order were cancelled
issues.fix: Reword the correct option to "It only tries an order the method is allowed to cancel".
